news.headline: Dow Tops 51,000 First Time Ever; S&P 500 Clinches 9th Straight Weekly Gain
news.body: U.S. stocks closed Friday May 29 at all-time highs, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average surging 0.7% above the 51,000 milestone for the first time and the S&P 500 rising 0.2% to 7,580 to seal a ninth consecutive weekly advance — its longest winning streak since 2023. The Nasdaq added 0.3% and closed May up 8%, capping what analysts called one of the strongest two-month stretches since 2020. The nine-week rally was driven by AI earnings validation from Dell, Snowflake, and Micron, easing oil prices on U.S.-Iran ceasefire optimism, and a PCE inflation print that came in slightly below expectations. The Russell 2000 was the lone laggard, slipping 0.6%, while Treasuries posted their best week since the U.S.-Iran war began.

news.headline: ServiceNow Surges 14% as Dell AI Shock Triggers Enterprise Software Re-Rating
news.body: ServiceNow stock posted its largest single-session gain in over a year, surging 14.4%, as Dell's blowout AI infrastructure print triggered a broad reassessment of enterprise software valuations. ServiceNow had separately beaten its own Q1 2026 estimates, delivering EPS of $0.97 vs. consensus of $0.80 and revising full-year 2026 subscription revenue guidance to $15.74B–$15.78B, implying ~22% YoY growth. Analysts characterized NOW's AI governance and workflow automation layer as directly in the path of accelerating enterprise AI spending. The move lifted the broader IGV software ETF and peers including CrowdStrike (+8.9%) and Palantir (+9.2%).

news.headline: Dell Q1 FY27 Shocks Wall Street: AI Server Revenue Surges 757%, Stock +33%
news.body: Dell Technologies reported Q1 FY27 revenue of $43.8B vs. consensus of $35.77B and adjusted EPS of $4.86 vs. $2.96 expected, driven by $16.1B in AI server revenue and $24.4B in new AI orders. Management raised full-year revenue guidance by $27B to $165B–$169B and hiked FY27 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.90 from $12.90, including a $60B AI server sales forecast. Shares surged ~33% for their best single session on record, with the company carrying a record $51.3B AI-related backlog. Multiple analysts sharply raised price targets, with Barclays moving to $550 and Bernstein to $500.

news.headline: Costco Q3 Sales Jump 11.6% to $69.15B on Record Gas Volumes; Stock Slips on Slim EPS Miss
news.body: Costco (NASDAQ: COST) reported fiscal Q3 2026 net sales of $69.15 billion, up 11.6% year-over-year, and total revenue of $70.53 billion, topping the consensus estimate, driven by record-breaking gasoline volumes as Middle East-driven fuel prices pushed new shoppers to Costco pumps. Net income rose 15.2% to $2.19 billion, or $4.93 per diluted share, and comparable sales climbed 9.8%, including 21.5% growth in digitally-enabled channels. However, the adjusted EPS of $4.93 narrowly missed some analyst estimates of $4.97–$4.98, and gross margins were slightly compressed, enough to trigger valuation discipline in a stock trading near 52x earnings. Shares closed around $995, down about 0.85%, as the market signaled that merely strong results are insufficient to justify further multiple expansion at current levels.

news.headline: Snowflake Surges 36% on Blowout Q1, $6B AWS Deal Counters 'SaaSpocalypse' Fears
news.body: Snowflake reported Q1 fiscal revenue of $1.39B (+33.5% YoY), beating estimates of $1.32B, with adjusted EPS of $0.39 vs. $0.32 expected, while AI accounts on its platform grew from 9,100 to 13,600 in one quarter. The company simultaneously announced a $6B multi-year compute partnership with AWS leveraging Graviton and AI GPU technologies, and raised full-year product revenue guidance by $180M. Shares closed 36% higher in their best day ever, sparking a broad software rally with ServiceNow +14%, Palantir +9%, and Oracle +6%. The results directly challenged the prevailing 'SaaSpocalypse' narrative that AI would destroy legacy SaaS business models.

news.headline: Samsung Hits ₩2,000T Market Cap as HBM4E Debut Drives KOSPI to Record 8,476
news.body: Samsung Electronics surged over 5% on May 29 after announcing the world's first shipment of 12-layer HBM4E samples to global customers including Nvidia, AMD, and Google — pulled forward by six months from the originally planned H2 2026 timeline. The chip delivers a 20%+ speed improvement over HBM4 and positions Samsung ahead of SK Hynix and Micron, whose own HBM4E samples are slated for H2. Samsung's market cap crossed 2,000 trillion won for the first time, a milestone for the Korean market. The KOSPI closed up 3% at a fresh record of 8,476.15, with Korea Investment & Securities setting a 570,000-won target on Samsung, implying ~80% further upside.
news.source: Reuters / Korea Herald / Seoul Economic Daily

news.headline: Lenovo Surges 22% on HSI to Record HK$24 After Blowout AI Earnings; Stock Doubles in May
news.body: Lenovo Group (0992.HK) jumped ~22% on May 29 to HK$24.00, capping a 109% gain for the month of May after the company reported Q4 revenue of $21.6 billion (+27% YoY) with net profit up 479% YoY, driven by its Infrastructure Solutions division growing 37% on AI server demand. AI-related revenue surged 84% and now represents 38% of total sales. The stock hit an all-time high and is the top Hang Seng constituent YTD with a 159% gain, more than triple the second-best performer. The Hang Seng Index recovered 0.7% on the day, with Lenovo the single largest positive contributor.

news.headline: Japan's Topix Hits All-Time Record, Nikkei +2.5% as MLCC Stocks Surge 12–20%
news.body: Japan's Topix rose 1.41% to an all-time high of 3,957.17 on May 29, while the Nikkei 225 gained 2.53% to 66,329.5, driven by a broad surge in semiconductor-related components. Silicon wafer maker SUMCO soared ~19.3%, Taiyo Yuden gained ~13.9%, Murata Manufacturing rose ~12.7%, and substrate maker Ibiden jumped ~16.5%, following brokerage upgrades that raised H2 2026 demand forecasts for MLCCs and silicon wafers used in AI servers. SoftBank Group added 5.1% on AI sentiment. Tailwinds also included softer-than-expected Tokyo CPI (1.3%) and an upside surprise in Japan's April retail sales and industrial production.
news.source: CNBC / TradingEconomics / Japan Stock Intel / TradingKey

news.headline: DRAM May Contract Price Breaches $20 Mark for First Time; TrendForce Flags Q3 Uptrend
news.body: TrendForce published its May 2026 DRAM contract price update on May 29, confirming prices broke the $20 threshold for the first time — recording the steepest monthly gain of the year — as AI server restocking and low supplier inventories sustain strong pricing power. PC DRAM contract prices rose significantly in Q2 and the upward trend is projected to extend through Q3 and Q4 2026. The data directly benefits Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, the dominant DRAM suppliers whose combined KOSPI weighting exceeds 42%, amplifying index sensitivity to the memory supercycle. The print reinforces buy cases across the Korean and Japanese semiconductor supply chains.

news.headline: Asia Markets Rebound as US-Iran Agree 60-Day Ceasefire Extension; Hang Seng -1.3% on Prior Day
news.body: Asian equity markets rallied on May 29 after overnight reports confirmed Washington and Tehran agreed to a 60-day extension of their ceasefire and began nuclear talks, with a White House official citing a deal that also pointed to possible unrestricted Strait of Hormuz shipping resumption. The KOSPI gained 3%+, the Nikkei 225 added 2.53%, and the Hang Seng recovered 0.7%, partially reversing its 1.3% drop the prior session when escalating U.S. strikes and Iranian missile activity near Kuwait had rattled regional sentiment. Oil prices edged lower on the deal, relieving pressure on energy-import-dependent Japan and South Korea. The ceasefire extension also spilled into Wall Street record closes overnight, reinforcing the Asia open.

news.headline: Wheat Hits 5-Week Low as USDA Flags Record-Small Winter Harvest; Grains Extend Slide
news.body: Chicago wheat futures tumbled to a low since May 8, closing at $6.10½/bu on May 29 — a fifth consecutive daily decline — after USDA projected the 2026-27 US winter wheat harvest at just 1.048 billion bushels, the smallest since 1965, down 25% year-over-year due to persistent Southern Plains dryness. Corn also fell 9 cents to $4.46¾/bu and soybeans dropped 7¾ cents to $11.86¾/bu as the market unwound war-risk premiums tied to improving Iran ceasefire prospects that had briefly supported ag complex prices. Soybean export data remained bearish, with 2025-26 US cumulative shipments down 21% year-on-year and tracking a 13-year low. Forecast weekend rains for Kansas and Nebraska offered limited price support ahead of the June acreage report.

news.headline: Gold Climbs to $4,580/oz on Iran Ceasefire Hopes, Logs Monthly Decline
news.body: Gold rose for a second straight session to $4,580/oz on May 29 as reports of a tentative US-Iran 60-day ceasefire extension lifted risk appetite, though the metal remained on track for a ~0.8% monthly loss. Bullion has faced persistent headwinds since late February as the Iran-driven oil price surge fuelled inflation concerns, with April US CPI showing the fastest rise in three years and reinforcing Fed rate-on-hold expectations well into 2027. Demand signals from Asia were muted: Indian demand stayed weak on high prices and import duties while Chinese consumer premiums narrowed. Prices closed the month at $4,576 per CFTC settlement data, well below the January 2026 peak above $5,400.

news.headline: US Nat Gas Hits 3-Month High on Below-Forecast EIA Storage Build
news.body: US natural gas futures climbed above $3.30/MMBtu — the highest since early February and up over 20% in four weeks — after the EIA reported a 92 bcf storage injection for the week ended May 22, below the 95–96 bcf consensus and well under the 104 bcf year-ago build. The tighter-than-expected injection narrowed the seasonal surplus to 144 bcf above the five-year average, down from 149 bcf the prior week. Additional support came from updated weather forecasts showing above-average temperatures across the western US June 1–10, boosting air-conditioning power demand expectations. LNG export flows to major terminals also eased due to seasonal maintenance, tightening near-term supply further.

news.headline: Brent Posts Worst Monthly Loss Since 2020 on US-Iran 60-Day Ceasefire MOU
news.body: Brent crude fell ~19% in May to below $91/bbl — its steepest monthly decline since the Covid-19 pandemic — after US officials confirmed negotiators agreed a 60-day memorandum of understanding to extend the ceasefire and open the Strait of Hormuz, pending Trump's sign-off. The Strait has been effectively closed since March, choking roughly 20% of global seaborne oil and LNG supply, with WTI settling near $87/bbl. Markets are pricing in eventual supply restoration, though analysts at UBS noted crude loadings inside the Gulf remain "extremely low" and infrastructure damage means any recovery will be gradual. The deal still requires Trump's formal approval and Iranian acceptance of nuclear and mine-clearing conditions.

news.headline: Copper Slips Below $6.25/lb as Iran Peace Talks Cloud Sulfur Supply Outlook
news.body: Copper futures fell from a one-week high of $6.40/lb to below $6.25/lb after Iran rejected a US claim of an unofficial Hormuz shipping agreement, introducing fresh uncertainty over the restoration of sulfur and sulfuric acid flows from GCC producers critical to copper smelting. China had already moved to suspend copper anode exports due to tight domestic supply of heap-leach inputs, underscoring how the Strait of Hormuz closure had cascaded into base metals production chains. Prices had been underpinned earlier in the week by AI-driven data center demand expectations but lost momentum as geopolitical uncertainty persisted. Analysts flagged that restored sulfur access from Gulf producers remains a necessary precondition for a durable copper supply recovery.
